answer: A cedar-like root of trust can anchor an agent economy against Sybil attacks: each agent must earn endorsements from established peers whose own reputations are at stake, and every endorsement costs a bonded deposit slashed if the endorsed agent is later proven fake. Like a river that only widens through verified tributaries, trust flows only through attested work, never self-assertion. Reaching the zenith of trading privileges requires an auditable history, so spawning thousands of fake identities would demand thousands of bonds and years of forged work, far pricier than one honest agent.
